title: bug: wrapper hot-reload exec's the on-disk script without a syntax check, so a half-edited moe-agent.sh kills every seat that reloads
description:
scripts/moe-agent.sh:6043-6065 (the "wrapper source changed on disk; restarting to load it" block) checks only the sha256 of $MOE_WRAPPER_PATH. When it changes, the wrapper deregisters the seat (reason wrapper_restart) and runs `exec "$MOE_WRAPPER_PATH" "${MOE_WRAPPER_ARGV[@]}"`. No `bash -n` runs first. The fallback line "wrapper relaunch failed; continuing on current bytes" is reached only if exec itself fails, never when the new script fails to parse. The ps1 supervisor has the equivalent hot-reload path.

Seats launched with the project path run the shared checkout's own copy (observed 2026-10-25: 70+ processes on /mnt/d/projexts/moes/scripts/moe-agent.sh). So whenever a task edits the wrapper in place (c532d223 was doing so at 10:52Z, +42/-9 dirty), every wrapper that reaches its loop top re-execs the in-progress bytes. If those bytes are mid-edit and unparseable, the seat dies after it has already deregistered.

Expected: before re-exec, validate the new bytes (`bash -n` for sh; [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile with zero errors for ps1). On failure, log a loud MOE_WRAPPER_RELOAD_REFUSED-style line, stay on the current bytes without deregistering, and retry on a later iteration only when the hash changes again. Keep both launchers in parity (parity-check lists the new code), and add a postflight arm with an unparseable wrapper copy.
definitionOfDone: When the on-disk wrapper changes to bytes that fail `bash -n` (sh) or ParseFile (ps1), the running wrapper does not deregister or exec, logs a refusal line naming the reason, and keeps serving on its current bytes; a later change to parseable bytes reloads normally.
Both postflight harnesses gain an arm with an unparseable wrapper copy that proves the seat survives and stays registered, plus the existing [hot reload] arm stays green.
`bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh` (and the ps1 twin) pass with any new code/banner registered in both checkers.
Fresh `MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh` and the ps1 twin exit 0, with output supplied to complete_task.

implementationPlan.description:
TESTS FIRST, bash harness (scripts/tests/postflight.sh: LF, runs under `set -euo pipefail`). Load test-driven-development. EDIT WITH CLAUDE'S Edit/Write TOOLS ONLY (contested path; see risks).

Add a new arm right after the existing `[hot reload] ok:` echo (~line 1949) and before `# --- Quality gate (settings.qualityGate)`. Header comment: twin of the refused-reload arm in postflight.ps1; seats launched from the shared checkout reload every edit of the real file, and a half-applied edit used to make each of them deregister and exec bytes bash could not parse.

Reuse the existing arm's helpers by re-pointing their globals at a FRESH copy. reload_seq, reload_fail and reload_wait resolve RELOAD_PROJECT, reload_pid and the out file at call time.
- RELOAD_DIR="$TMP_DIR/reload-refused", plus RELOAD_PROJECT and RELOAD_WRAPPER under it.
- Same fixture as the existing arm: cp -R "$ROOT_DIR/scripts", chmod +x, project.json with autoCommit false, an empty chan-general.jsonl, and daemon.json (moe-call.sh refuses to deregister without it).
- Same launch line, with --worker-id worker-reload-refused, writing to the SAME $TMP_DIR/wrapper-reload.out. The first arm has finished with that file, and reload_fail prints it.
- Same LIVE_PIDS bookkeeping.

Sequence:
(1) `reload_wait 0 '^c'`, then record k = the number of claims so far.
(2) The refused edit is an APPEND: `printf 'if true; then :\n' >> "$RELOAD_WRAPPER"`. Measured at planning: `bash -n` then fails with '<path>: line N: syntax error: unexpected end of file', rc 2. Use appends, never a whole-file rewrite: a short append is effectively atomic, but a rewrite can be hashed half-written and log a second refusal.
(3) `reload_wait 0 "^c{$((k + 3)),}\$"`. Three claims after the edit guarantee that at least two loop tops saw the refused bytes. EDITS=0 makes any wrapper_restart fail fast, and kill -0 catches a dead seat.
(4) The parseable edit: `printf 'fi\n' >> "$RELOAD_WRAPPER"`. The tail `if true; then :` + `fi` parses, and it would only run after the main loop ends.
(5) `reload_wait 1 '^c+rc'`.
(6) Kill the wrapper and restore LIVE_PIDS. Then assert on the final state; each failure goes through reload_fail with a message naming the broken promise:
  - the sequence matches ^c+rc+$ ('a refused edit must not deregister; the next parseable edit reloads once');
  - `grep -c MOE_WRAPPER_RELOAD_REFUSED` (with `|| true`) is exactly 1 ('one refusal line per refused hash, got N');
  - ONE `grep -Eq` (no pipe: under pipefail a `| grep -q` can read SIGPIPE as failure) for 'MOE_WRAPPER_RELOAD_REFUSED: wrapper source changed on disk but does not parse; staying on the current bytes until it changes again: .*moe-agent\.sh'. bash prefixes its own message with the script path, so this proves the reason is bash -n's and stays locale-proof;
  - 'restarting to load it' appears exactly once.
Then echo '[hot reload refused] ok: refused once, stayed registered, reloaded on the next parseable edit'.

RED proof, in a scratch copy of scripts/ (never the live tree). Build an arm-only harness by anchors, per mem pattern-postflight-red-proof-via-temp-tree: [0, `FROZEN_SUITE="$TMP_DIR/frozen-candidate.cjs"`) + [`# --- Hot reload: the wrapper re-execs itself`, `# --- Quality gate (settings.qualityGate)`) + `echo PASS`. Run it against the CURRENT wrapper. Expected: the existing arm passes, and the new arm fails with reload_wait's 'a restart with no edit behind it'. The old wrapper deregisters and execs. Because bash parses incrementally, the exec'd copy with a broken tail keeps running, so the forbidden deregister is the observable. Put both lines in the step note. Keep the generator; steps 2 and 7 reuse it.

implementationPlan.description:
Bash twin fix (scripts/moe-agent.sh, LF). Develop it and prove it in the step-1 scratch tree FIRST: the arm subset must go GREEN against the fixed scratch copy. Only then port it to the live file.

1. Next to `MOE_WRAPPER_LAUNCH_HASH=""` (~line 6011), add `MOE_WRAPPER_REFUSED_HASH=""`, the hash of bytes already refused.
2. Loop-top restart check (~6043):
  - Add `&& [ "$MOE_WRAPPER_CURRENT_HASH" != "$MOE_WRAPPER_REFUSED_HASH" ]` to the change test.
  - Then, BEFORE the restart announcement, stop_heartbeat_sidecar, the deregister, the SECURE_TEMP_DIR removal and the exec: `MOE_WRAPPER_PARSE_RC=0; MOE_WRAPPER_PARSE_ERR="$(bash -n "$MOE_WRAPPER_PATH" 2>&1)" || MOE_WRAPPER_PARSE_RC=$?`. This is the error handling that matters here: the `||` keeps set -e from killing the seat on the very failure this guards. Both idioms were verified at planning.
  - Non-zero rc:
    - set MOE_WRAPPER_REFUSED_HASH="$MOE_WRAPPER_CURRENT_HASH";
    - cut the error to its first line with `${MOE_WRAPPER_PARSE_ERR%%$'\n'*}`, falling back to `bash -n exited <rc>` when it is empty;
    - print to stderr, exactly: `[WARN] MOE_WRAPPER_RELOAD_REFUSED: wrapper source changed on disk but does not parse; staying on the current bytes until it changes again: <reason>`;
    - fall through, so this iteration serves as usual: no continue, no sidecar stop, no deregister, no temp-dir removal.
  - Zero rc: today's restart body, byte-for-byte, in the else branch.
3. Add a short why-comment: a seat launched from the shared checkout reloads every edit of this file, and a half-applied edit used to cost it its registration and then its process; refuse such bytes once per hash and keep serving the bytes already parsed. Do NOT repeat the code token or the refusal prose in any comment: the parity needles must stay unique to the emitting line.
4. Use `bash -n` on the real path. Do not validate and exec a temp copy: that would move BASH_SOURCE/SCRIPT_DIR, which moe-call.sh, the mods and the *.mjs helpers resolve against.

LIVE-FILE DISCIPLINE. Every seat launched from this checkout hot-reloads each write, and until this lands they have no guard. Make exactly two Claude Edit calls, each one self-contained:
- (a) the init line;
- (b) the whole `if [ -n "$MOE_WRAPPER_CURRENT_HASH" ] ... fi` block.
Run `bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh` right after each one. Then `diff` the scratch copy against the live file: it must differ only by peer hunks, if there are any. Rerun the step-1 subset GREEN with the live bytes, and record its output as this step's test evidence.

implementationPlan.description:
PowerShell twin fix (scripts/moe-agent.ps1: UTF-8 BOM + LF; afterwards ef bb bf and zero CR bytes). Develop it in the step-3 scratch tree FIRST, until the subset is GREEN on both engines.

1. Next to `$script:MoeWrapperLaunchHash = $null` (~line 5455), add `$script:MoeWrapperRefusedHash = $null`.
2. Loop-top restart check (~5493):
  - Add `-and $moeCurrentHash -ne $script:MoeWrapperRefusedHash` to the change test.
  - Then, before the announcement: `$moeParseReason = ''; try { $moeParseErrors = $null; $null = [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile($script:MoeWrapperPath, [ref]$null, [ref]$moeParseErrors); if ($moeParseErrors.Count -gt 0) { $moeParseReason = "line $($moeParseErrors[0].Extent.StartLineNumber): $($moeParseErrors[0].Message)" } } catch { $moeParseReason = "ParseFile failed: $($_.Exception.Message)" }`. Error handling: the catch always yields a NON-empty reason, so an IO error is a refusal and never a reload; nothing here can escape to $ErrorActionPreference='Stop'. ParseFile is the engine's own reader, BOM/ANSI decoding included, so it judges exactly what the supervisor's `&` would parse.
  - Non-empty reason: `$script:MoeWrapperRefusedHash = $moeCurrentHash`, then `Write-Host "[WARN] MOE_WRAPPER_RELOAD_REFUSED: wrapper source changed on disk but does not parse; staying on the current bytes until it changes again: $moeParseReason" -ForegroundColor Yellow`. Fall through to serve the iteration: no Stop-HeartbeatSidecar, no Invoke-MoeDeregister, no MoeWrapperRelaunchRequested, no break.
  - Empty reason: today's body unchanged, in the else branch. Its continue and break still target the do loop.
3. Supervisor catch comment (~line 89): a parse failure can now reach it only when the bytes changed again after the restart check, or the file rejects the bound parameters, or it is gone. Say so without naming the code token.
Use the same why-comment rules as step 2.

LIVE-FILE DISCIPLINE: one self-contained Edit each for the init line, the restart-check block and the comment. After EACH Edit, run ParseFile on the live file under BOTH powershell.exe and pwsh.exe (0 errors), plus the BOM/CR test. Then rerun the step-3 subset GREEN on both engines.

implementationPlan.description:
ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW with mutation proof (load adversarial-self-review). Post it as a task comment, then complete_task with the step-6 output.

Attack your own diff:
(1) The refusal path must not touch the seat: no deregister, no sidecar stop, no temp-dir removal, no exec, break or continue, and nothing that set -e or $ErrorActionPreference='Stop' can turn into an exit.
(2) Once per hash: a second, different bad hash logs again; bad bytes reverted to the launch bytes do nothing; bad then good reloads exactly once. Trace each case through the code.
(3) Cost is paid only when the hash moved: about 15 ms for bash -n and about 50 ms for ParseFile, measured.
(4) TOCTOU: bytes that change again between the check and the exec or the supervisor's `&` are not re-checked. The window is about the deregister RPC. State it; add no machinery.

comments.content:
Adversarial self-review (step 7), done on `git diff 16ec9f9 -- <the six files>`.

(1) The refusal path leaves the seat alone.
- sh: rc != 0 does only three things: record MOE_WRAPPER_REFUSED_HASH, keep the first error line, and echo the [WARN] to stderr. It then falls out of both ifs into the normal iteration. It does not call stop_heartbeat_sidecar, deregister, rm SECURE_TEMP_DIR, exec or continue.
- sh under `set -e` (line 5): `ERR="$(bash -n ...)" || RC=$?` is the only command that can fail, and `||` guards it. The `%%$'\n'*` trim is a plain assignment.
- ps1: ParseFile sits inside try/catch, and the catch always sets a non-empty reason. Under $ErrorActionPreference='Stop' nothing escapes, so an IO error is a refusal, never a reload. The refusal branch does not call Stop-HeartbeatSidecar, Invoke-MoeDeregister, RelaunchRequested, break or continue. The else branch is today's body; its continue and break still target the do loop.

(2) Once per hash, traced through the code:
- Bad H1: refused, memo = H1, and the next loops skip it silently.
- A different bad H2: it differs from the memo, so it is parsed, refused and logged again.
- H1 reverted to the launch bytes: equal to the launch hash, so nothing happens.
- H1 back again after that: already refused, still unparseable, so it is skipped silently. That is correct.
- Bad, then good H3: it differs from the memo, parses, and restarts exactly once. The exec'd or rerun pass resets the memo and captures H3 as its launch hash.
The arms assert exactly one refusal line and exactly one restart.

(3) Cost: the check runs only when the sha256, already computed each iteration, moves. Re-measured `bash -n` on the 8.5k-line file: 35 ms wall. ParseFile was 47-59 ms at planning on PS 5.1 and pwsh 7.

(4) TOCTOU (accepted residual, no machinery added):
- Bytes that change again between the check and the exec or the supervisor's `&` are not re-checked. The window is about one deregister RPC.
- A torn write that happens to parse is not caught. `bash -n` and ParseFile judge syntax, not meaning.
- A transient failure of the check itself (a fork failure, a sharing violation) refuses those bytes until the hash moves again. That is fail-safe.
- `bash -n` uses the default shopts; the wrapper sets none.

(5) The existing [hot reload] arm is unchanged and green in the gate on all three engines.

(6) Encoding:
- moe-agent.ps1 and postflight.ps1: BOM ef bb bf.
- parity-check.ps1: still no BOM.
- All six files: 0 CR bytes.
- The parity needles occur only on sh:6059 and ps1:5521.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
(a) CHOSEN: before the restart, check the on-disk path with `bash -n` (sh) and Parser::ParseFile (ps1), and refuse once per hash. These are the DoD's exact checks. ParseFile is the engine's own reader (BOM/ANSI decoding included), so it judges what the supervisor's `&` will parse.
(b) Validate a temp copy, then exec or run THAT copy. Rejected: BASH_SOURCE, SCRIPT_DIR and $PSCommandPath would point into temp (moe-call.sh, the mods and the *.mjs helpers resolve beside the wrapper), and the next hash check would read a different file.
(c) Re-check inside the ps1 supervisor, or after exec. Rejected: by then the pass has exited and the seat has deregistered, so there are no current bytes left to stay on.
(d) Re-parse on every iteration. Rejected: the DoD wants a retry only when the hash changes, and 70+ seats would each log on every poll.
(e) Post the refusal to #general. Rejected: one console line per seat per bad hash is enough; a chat post would be 70+ messages per bad edit.
(f) Hash, parse, re-hash, and defer when the hash moved. Rejected: machinery for a sub-second check-to-exec window, when edits arrive seconds to minutes apart. It is documented as a residual instead.
(g) Split sh and ps1 into two tasks. Rejected: the DoD makes them one deliverable (parity registers both), and the parity edits are one line each. Six files is the daemon's soft-warning band, not a reject.

sh (scripts/moe-agent.sh):
- Restart check: ~6043-6068. The launch hash is captured once, at ~6010-6016, before the main while loop.
